llm.summary: The skill's instructions, requirements, and optional installation steps align with a 'daily book' oracle: it calls an external API for a book, has no extra env/credentials, and the install suggestions are limited to scheduling and local skill config — review the external API and cron behavior before enabling automated pushes.

dimensions.detail: The name/description and runtime instructions consistently implement a 'Book of the Day' oracle: fetch a book from an API, format a short poetic reading, and end with a specified CTA. No unrelated binaries, credentials, or surprising capabilities are requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions tell the agent to GET {BOOK_OF_THE_DAY_API_URL} (default https://book-of-the-day.vercel.app) and to format the response; this is coherent. Two minor notes: (1) the skill requires 'never reuse a book' which implies the agent maintain or check state (e.g., by writing/reading its own config or memory) — not spelled out but plausible; (2) the default API is an external endpoint of unknown operator (no homepage provided), so callers should consider whether requests (date and possibly language/context) are acceptable to send there.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no automated install spec embedded in the skill bundle (instruction-only). INSTALL.md suggests using the platform's 'clawhub install' and adding a cron job via openclaw — these are platform-native commands rather than arbitrary downloads. No archived downloads or external installers from unknown hosts are embedded in the skill itself.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables or credentials. INSTALL.md mentions writing BOOK_OF_THE_DAY_API_URL into the user's ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json if needed — that is a reasonable, limited configuration change for a skill. No unrelated secrets or wide-ranging env access are requested.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and normal model invocation are set. The INSTALL.md shows an optional cron push (scheduling daily messages to configured channels) and instructs editing the user's OpenClaw skill config; these are expected for a push-style skill but are meaningful persistence/automation decisions — enable only if you want automated outbound messages to your channels. The skill does not request global config edits beyond its own entry.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill is internally consistent with its stated purpose, but check two things before installing: (1) Trustworthiness of the external API — the skill calls https://book-of-the-day.vercel.app (or a URL you set). If you don't trust that host, supply your own BOOK_OF_THE_DAY_API_URL or host a private instance. Understand that the request will include at least a date parameter (and may include language headers), so the external server will see those calls. (2) Automated pushes — the INSTALL.md shows an optional cron that will post '今日之书' to configured channels (Telegram/Slack). Only enable that if you want scheduled outbound messages and ensure your OpenClaw channel integrations are configured securely. Finally, be aware the skill may write its config into ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json to store the API URL or state (e.g., to avoid reusing books); review that file if you want to audit stored state.
